entries.title: Venus phases desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a Venus page: a top-down Sun, Venus, and Earth on circular orbits. Play or scrub from a schematic inferior conjunction and the disk runs crescent through gibbous — evening star, morning star, and the far-side near-full. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not a finder chart.

entries.title: Retrograde desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a retrograde page: a top-down Sun, Earth, and Mars on circular orbits. Play or scrub and Earth laps the outer planet. A line of sight and a longitude strip show the backward loop — prograde, stationary, retrograde — while both orbit arrows keep going the same way. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris and not for pointing a telescope.

entries.title: No Man's Sky moodboard
entries.blurb: The material graph is now three desks. The moodboard is a dense grid — minerals, gases, plants, earth, and early components. Click to open, mark several, and star a short list that stays in this browser. Refine stays the edge explorer. The planner is a stub that reads those pins. Craft rows are station inventory. High-speed sublimation is the three-slot path to nitrogen salt, enriched carbon, and thermic condensate. Wiring loom stays buy-only. Community ratios — a patch can change a recipe.

entries.title: Game guides — No Man's Sky bases
entries.blurb: Game guides opens at /game/guides/, separate from the playable /games/ pages. First tool: a No Man's Sky base map. Load exported JSON or a Steam save.hg in the browser, plot planetary bases on a schematic disk, and mark the Euclid Hub capital at Uthmi Beta. Zoom toward the pointer or the selected base; same-system piles spread apart and show their names. Freighter bases stay listed aside. Nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Tides desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a tides page: a top-down Earth with exaggerated ocean bulges. Slide the Moon from new to full and the label switches from spring to neap. A light spin shows two highs per turn under bulges that stay put. Cited NASA and NOAA. Schematic, not a tide table — and not a Campbell harbor guide.

entries.title: Eclipses desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows an eclipses page: a side-view Sun, Earth, and Moon on a tilted orbit. Toggle solar or lunar, then slide the node offset from aligned to about 5° and watch the shadow miss. Umbra, penumbra, nodes, eclipse seasons. Cited NASA. Schematic, not a prediction.

entries.title: Seasons day length
entries.blurb: The seasons desk adds day length by latitude — a slider from pole to pole, tied to the same day-of-year control. Near equinox the strip stays near 12 hours; solstice stretches toward the poles. Classroom hour-angle math, not a sunrise almanac.

entries.title: Seasons desk
entries.blurb: Astronomy grows a seasons page: walk the year, keep Earth’s axis parallel at about 23.4°, and see which hemisphere leans into the Sun. Perihelion is early January — Northern winter. Cited NASA. Schematic, not an ephemeris or a forecast.

entries.title: Humanoid robots status essay
entries.blurb: Science robotics grows a nested 2025–2026 stand: Figure Helix 2.5 in unseen homes, electric Atlas and Digit 5 on industrial floors, Optimus production talk labeled as plans. Cited. Company claims and supply-chain reports can outrun verified deployments.

entries.title: Weather wind direction
entries.blurb: The weather desk now shows wind direction with speed — compass point and degrees from Open-Meteo (direction the wind blows from).

entries.title: Electromagnetic spectrum desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a radio-to-gamma literacy page: tap the bands for classroom wavelength and frequency ranges, then slide a Wien’s-law peak (Sun ~5800 K near visible). Cited NASA / Imagine the Universe. Not a lab instrument or medical advice.

entries.title: Text tools desk
entries.blurb: Tools grows a character counter with live words/lines/UTF-8 bytes, case convert, trim, sort, dedupe, copy, and download. Runs in the browser — nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Wallpapers desk
entries.blurb: Free desktop wallpapers with in-browser cover-crop downloads — original, common sizes, and custom W×H. First image: Pacific Northwest Coast at Golden Hour (Grok Imagine / AI-generated; native 1792×1008, larger sizes labeled upscales).

entries.title: Annual Dial text backup
entries.blurb: Save day marks from the Annual Dial as a readable .txt, then restore that file — replace or merge — so entries survive a cleared browser and can move between devices. Local only; nothing is uploaded.

entries.title: Standard Model desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a particle-physics literacy page: clickable quark / lepton / boson grid, generations, force diagram, and honest gaps (gravity, dark matter, neutrino mass). Cited CERN / Fermilab / PDG. Not a QFT course.

entries.title: Gravity desk
entries.blurb: Science grows a sibling literacy page for the force the Standard Model omits: everyday weight and orbits, Newton, Einstein / GPS, weakness vs other forces, and the quantum-gravity gap. Cited NASA / NIST / CERN. Not a theory of everything.

entries.title: Internet speed test
entries.blurb: Tools desk grows a browser speed test — ping, download, and upload against Cloudflare’s public edge. Approximate. Not a lab meter. Not affiliated with Cloudflare or Ookla.

entries.title: Solar map play speed
entries.blurb: Play on the solar system map now has a speed control — 0.5× through 10×, labeled in days per second. Date and local time stay the source of truth; share still uses ?date= and ?time=.

entries.title: Solar map day & time
entries.blurb: The solar system map now takes a local day and time — planets sit at approximate mean heliocentric longitudes for that moment. Schematic, not a JPL ephemeris. Share with ?date= and ?time=.
